generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL. For tables with compact rows, start above the compact max so compact keys are preserved.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the parent table's key pool (compact + generated keys actually present in the instance); ~7% of child rows get NULL only when the FK column is nullable; otherwise all rows reference an existing parent. Reserve at least one parent key per parent table to remain unreferenced (parent_rows_without_children).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in the observed range; include min, max, min-1 and max+1 as boundary probes where the semantic rule permits; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Draw from a small pool of realistic names; allow near-duplicates (case variants, one-character edits) at ~10% of rows; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_title: Draw from a pool of realistic titles; allow near-variants (case, truncation, one-char edit) at ~10% of rows; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_country: Draw from a small enum-like pool of country codes; allow case variants at ~10% of rows; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_generic: Draw from a small pool; allow near-duplicates at ~10%; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: 0.1 of rows per text column are fresh near-variants derived from base-pool values, not in the base pool.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_rule: For ORDER/LIMIT columns, ensure at least two rows share the top rank value; for COUNT(*)-based ties, control join cardinality so two parent rows have equal child counts. Plant ties by choosing existing child rows (never by appending ragged rows); if a tie cannot be planted on existing rows, append a full child row (all columns, valid FK/NULL values) to every column of the child table.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_rule: For DISTINCT columns, ensure 20-50% of rows (on the combined compact+generated data) are duplicates of another row's value; compute the share over the merged column and adjust generated values accordingly.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Every nullable column gets at least one NULL row; NULL share follows the compact database's share (0.0 observed, so use a small share ~5-10% to exercise NULL logic). Planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule; rules constrain only non-NULL operands. NULL injection is a deliberate deviation from the observed 0.0 null rate, permitted by the schema's nullability; rules are three-valued (NULL passes).
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_rule: Boundary probes are planted before NULL injection and before rule application; rule application must not overwrite planted boundary values (apply rules first, or exempt boundary values). Boundary values must survive as non-NULL in generated rows.
generic_sampling_rules.post_processing_rule: All post-processing keeps every column of a table the same length; guard against short/empty lists when planting ties or diversity. After build, verify: duplicate share and group-size distribution per targeted column over merged data; top-rank tie counts for Inst, Papers, Authors; presence of all boundary values as non-NULL; unreferenced-parent count per parent table.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: observed distinct countries; case-sensitive rule, 'usa' is a boundary probe that may be replaced by a valid enum value

supporting_evidence.authOrder_range: Authorship.authOrder distinct values are 1,2,3 (statistics); no 0 observed, so range 1-3.
supporting_evidence.country_enum: Inst.country distinct values are UK, USA, Japan, France (statistics).
supporting_evidence.pk_positive: All surrogate keys are positive integers in the sample rows.

uncertainty: The compact database shows null_rate 0.0 for all nullable columns; NULL shares are set small (~5-10%) to exercise NULL logic without contradicting the observed statistics. NULL injection is intentional and permitted by the schema's nullability; rules are three-valued (NULL passes). authOrder=0 is not a valid value (BETWEEN 1 AND 3); the boundary target lists only 1,2,3, and these must appear as non-NULL in generated rows (reserve rows for boundary probes before NULL injection). Inst.country and Authorship.authOrder are declared nullable but observed non-NULL; NULLs are permitted by the schema. The Inst.name boundary values are misspelled near-variants of 'Tohoku University' chosen to exercise equality/LIKE predicates; the Authors.lname/fname boundary values include fresh names (Ueno, Katsuhiro, Stephanie) consistent with the fresh_value_share rule. The IN rule for Inst.country is case-sensitive, so 'usa' is a boundary probe that may be replaced by a valid enum value; if the program enforces the IN rule strictly, 'usa' will not survive. table_sizes_per_instance are minimums; the program may add up to 6 extra rows per table. COUNT-based ties must be planted for the exact (parent, child-count-column) pairs: Inst via Authorship.paperID, Papers via Authorship.paperID, Authors via Authorship.authID. Unreferenced parents must be provably unreferenced by both compact and generated child rows (add a fresh parent key above the compact max and never reference it).
